newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy 3rd mobile phone licence offered by June.
newsitem.headline: Italy 3rd mobile phone licence offered by June.

text.p: Italy will offer its third licence to operate a mobile telephone service for tender by June, deputy posts and telecommunications minister Michele Lauria said.
In a statement Lauria said Posts and Telecoms Minister Antonio Maccanico had sent a draft of urgent measures to Prime Minister Romano Prodi establishing the procedure for the licence tender.
The measures, which are due to be examined by the cabinet as soon as possible, will allow the start of the tender by June, Lauria said.
The measures also envisaged the introduction of a DECT (Digital European Cordless Telephony) supercordless telephone service for urban areas, the posts ministry statement said.
"The government confirms its willingness to proceed quickly with the start of the tender for choosing the third mobile phone operator," it said.
Italy's third mobile phone licence is expected to be for a PCN standard mobile phone service.

Several companies have expressed interested in competing for the licence including Italian broadcaster Mediaset together with British Telecom and Banca Nazionale del Lavoro, under their Albacom joint venture.
A newspaper reported this week that Deutsche Telekom was also interested in competing in conjunction with Italian state electricity utility Enel.
Italy currently has two GSM standard mobile phone service operators, state-controlled Telecom Italia Mobile (TIM) and Olivetti-controlled Omnitel Pronto Italia.
